title: The covenant of circumcision
hookLine: a baby boy's circumcision on the eighth day
last: A NEW LIFE IS GREETED WITH A BLESSING.

cards: A room full of people, on the eighth day after a birth: grandparents, cousins, a few friends who took the morning off. Near the front stands an empty chair that nobody sits in.

The baby is carried in on a pillow, and the room calls out: baruch haba. One person, a grandfather perhaps, or an honored friend, settles in to hold the child on his lap. Another, trained for exactly this, steps forward.
Then come blessings, a name spoken aloud for the first time, a little wine, and food.

teach.b: Brit milah. Brit means covenant; milah means circumcision. First, the command and its day.
In Genesis, in the chapter this path met in Lech Lecha, God makes a covenant with Abraham, to be carried in the body: "And he that is eight days old shall be circumcised among you."
The eighth day is so central that the Talmud teaches it goes ahead even on Shabbat. But a baby's health comes first: if the child is unwell, the brit waits. Second, the people.
The one who performs it is called a mohel. The one who holds the baby is the sandak, a place of honor. And the empty chair belongs to Elijah the prophet.
Tradition says Elijah once complained that Israel had abandoned the covenant, so he is invited to every brit, to see for himself that it goes on. Third, the words.
The father, or both parents, bless God for the command to bring the child into the covenant of Abraham.

The guests answer with a line from the liturgy: as he has entered the covenant, so may he enter into Torah, the wedding canopy, and good deeds. Learning, love, kindness: a whole life, wished for in one breath.
Fourth, the name. At the brit, the boy's Hebrew name is announced for the first time, as son of his father, and in some families his mother too.
The covenant is the frame; the name is what goes inside it.

how: Many Jewish families hold a brit milah on the eighth day after a boy's birth, with a mohel performing the circumcision, a sandak holding the baby, blessings, the announcement of his Hebrew name, and a festive meal.

games.q: you're a guest. the blessing for the covenant has just been said. what does the room answer?
o: a wish for wealth and a long life.
as he entered the covenant, may he enter Torah, the canopy and good deeds.
games.why: the guests wish him Torah, the wedding canopy and good deeds: learning, love and kindness in one line.

practice: Walk through a brit in your mind, one step per breath: the baby carried in and the room saying baruch haba, Elijah's empty chair, the sandak holding, the blessing, the guests' wish for Torah, the canopy and good deeds, and the name.
Then let the last image rest: a whole room promising to stand behind one small person. If you pray, you can pray for a child you love.

wordCard.voice: Brit milah. The covenant of circumcision: the eighth day, Elijah's chair, the guests' wish, and the name. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: the covenant. Eight days old, and already part of something very old. See you tomorrow.
